title: AEO for digital PR: How to build earned media presence that shows up in AI results
content:
Digital PR has always been about earning coverage that influences the audience you can’t reach through paid channels. While the value proposition of digital PR hasn’t changed, the definition of “showing up” has.
When buyers use answer engines to research a category, the brand that appears in those answers has earned a form of coverage that press releases and media lists weren’t designed to deliver. Earned media that appears in AI results now carries more influence than traditional coverage alone.
The PR teams pulling ahead are the ones treating AI visibility as a measurable outcome of their work — not something that happens downstream of traditional metrics.
The relationship between earned media and AI visibility is real, but it’s not uniform. For example, placement in a top-tier outlet doesn’t automatically translate into a citation in an answer engine. Some publications and content types generate citations at much higher rates than others.
If you’re measuring PR success solely by placement volume, domain authority, or estimated reach, you may be optimizing for metrics that no longer fully capture influence. The gap between traditional PR measurement and AI visibility is where accountability gets murky.
HubSpot AEO' s Citation Analysis surfaces which specific publications and content categories are generating citations in answer engines. PR teams can see which third-party publications are contributing to brand visibility and which aren’t. This makes it easier to evaluate which outlets and coverage types are worth prioritizing.
HubSpot’s marketing team recorded a 642% increase in citations for comparison articles and a 58% increase in overall mentions.
Knowing which placements are driving citations gives teams the data they need to target the publications that move their AI visibility score.
Not all media outlets are created equal in answer engines. Some media outlets are cited consistently; others rarely appear. PR teams need to understand which publications influence their category because it changes media outreach, content pitching, and relationship-building priorities.
Without that data, pitching strategy defaults to reach and reputation metrics that don’t reflect AI citation patterns. The result is effort spent on outlets that don’t move the needle on AI visibility, even when the coverage is objectively good.
HubSpot AEO' s Recommendations identify gaps in a business’s citation profile and flag the types of sources and content that are most likely to improve your brand visibility score. Teams can use those insights to build a more targeted media list and adjust their pitching strategy toward outlets with demonstrated citation influence.
Targeting the right outlets matters for AI visibility, but what ultimately counts is whether teams can connect that work to the business metrics PR is accountable for.
PR reporting has always involved a mix of quantitative and qualitative measures. AEO adds a cleaner signal: changes in the AI visibility score, citations, and share of voice are directly attributable to the content and placements driving them.
Teams that connect PR activity to AI visibility outcomes can make a stronger case to stakeholders for the value of earned media.
HubSpot AEO' s Brand Visibility Dashboard tracks brand visibility score, citations, and share of voice over time. As you run PR campaigns, you can track whether your visibility metrics shift. This gives you concrete data to connect earned media activity to AI visibility outcomes.
The publications that influence AI answers are largely the same outlets your team already builds relationships with. The difference is in knowing which placements to track, which to prioritize, and how to present the results in terms stakeholders can act on.

title: AEO for marketing agencies: How to deliver measurable AI visibility results for every client
content:
Clients are asking about AEO. Some have seen competitors show up in AI results and want to know what it means. Others have read that AI is changing how buyers find vendors and want to know what their agency is doing about it.
For marketing agencies, the challenge is delivering AEO at scale. Managing visibility tracking, content optimization, and performance reporting for 10 or 20 clients — each with different products, audiences, and competitive sets — is difficult to manage manually. To turn AEO into a sustainable service, agencies need a repeatable process and the right infrastructure.
Agencies that build AEO infrastructure now can make AEO part of their ongoing client services instead of treating every engagement as a one-off project.
When agencies manage AEO for a portfolio of clients, tracking each client’s brand visibility score, share of voice, and citations across multiple tools creates unnecessary work and is ultimately unsustainable.
Tool sprawl creates manual work and makes trends harder to spot. Teams end up spending time pulling data instead of using it to inform strategy. Using one tool consistently keeps benchmarking data clean.
HubSpot AEO ’s Brand Visibility Dashboard lets agencies track brand visibility score, citations, and share of voice in one place. Teams can monitor visibility trends, compare performance with competitors, and prioritize where to focus.
That visibility can also connect to broader marketing outcomes. According to HubSpot internal data, AEO users generate 2.6x more leads.
The goal is to turn AEO data into a repeatable process for improving each client’s visibility. The next step is to produce the content to close the identified gaps.
Once agencies know where a client’s visibility gaps are, the next step is creating or updating content to address them.
Getting cited in answer engines requires content that’s structured, authoritative, and aligned with the specific questions those engines are answering. That content can differ from traditional SEO, which means agencies need a way to identify the content opportunities that matter specifically for AI visibility.
Without a repeatable framework, producing citation-worthy content for multiple clients can feel like starting from scratch for every engagement. But with the right tooling in place, it becomes much easier to see which content changes are most likely to move the needle on visibility.
HubSpot AEO generates Recommendations tied to a client’s current visibility gaps and brand visibility score. Agencies can use those recommendations to brief writers, prioritize edits on existing pages, and build a content roadmap that directly targets visibility improvements. That gives teams a clearer connection between what they’re seeing in AI results and the content work they recommend to clients.
But creating and optimizing content is only part of the service. Agencies also need a simple way to show clients what changed.
Clients want to see progress. An AEO report gives agencies a concrete way to show it, whether that is citation counts, share of voice trends, and brand visibility score movement over time. These metrics turn an abstract concept into something agencies can bring to a monthly review meeting along with other marketing performance data.
The problem is that building those reports manually doesn’t scale. Pulling data from different sources for every account takes time and can lead to inconsistent reporting from one client to the next.
HubSpot AEO ’s Brand Visibility Dashboard gives marketing agencies exportable visibility data that agencies can use in client-facing reports. They can track changes over time and tie visibility improvements back to the content and outreach work they are doing. That makes reporting part of the AEO workflow instead of another manual task at the end of the month.
For agencies, scaling AEO is less about adding another service and more about building a repeatable system for delivering it.
HubSpot AEO helps agencies build that system by bringing together AI monitoring, content recommendations and creation based on visibility gaps, and reporting in one platform. Agencies can use that infrastructure to build AEO into their existing client workflows instead of managing every engagement from scratch.
Clients are already asking for AEO. The infrastructure to deliver it efficiently is what separates a reactive answer from a scalable practice.

title: Enterprise AEO: How to manage brand visibility at scale across products, segments, and markets
content:
Enterprise brand teams face a complex version of AEO that most tools weren’t built for. A single brand might span a dozen product lines, operate in multiple languages, and compete in markets where local answer engines have their own citation patterns.
When content teams, regional marketers, and product groups handle AEO separately, visibility becomes fragmented. The challenge becomes coordinating AEO across the organization. While individual teams may be able to see how individual product lines or markets are performing, they don’t have a clear picture of how the brand is showing up overall.
Scaling AEO at the enterprise level requires centralized monitoring, cross-team workflows, and the ability to tie visibility investments to revenue outcomes. Let’s get into each.
At the enterprise level, brand visibility across answer engines is a matrix, not a single number. Marketing teams need to understand how different product lines are cited, how visibility varies by region, and how the brand is positioned relative to competitors in each market. They also need to track those changes across answer engines.
When that data lives in disconnected tools or requires manual assembly, enterprise AEO monitoring quickly becomes difficult to scale. Teams end up with snapshots of individual products or markets but no way to see the full picture.
HubSpot AEO ’s Brand Visibility Dashboard consolidates brand visibility score, share of voice, and citations data across a brand’s entire footprint. Enterprise teams can segment visibility by product line or market and track trends across AI engines from one view.
The results speak for themselves: HubSpot AEO users generate 2.7x more MQLs, according to HubSpot internal data. This gives teams a way to connect AEO visibility with the broader marketing outcomes they already measure.
But monitoring visibility is only the first step. Enterprise teams also need a way to coordinate those insights and turn them into action.
Generating AEO recommendations is the easy part. The challenge is getting those recommendations acted on by content teams in multiple regions, working across different languages and editorial calendars.
Recommendations are ineffective when they sit in a dashboard that content teams don’t have access to, or arrive as ad hoc requests without priority or context. This creates a gap between identifying a visibility opportunity and actually acting on it.
Enterprise AEO requires coordinated action, not just data. HubSpot AEO surfaces recommendations based on a company’s current visibility gaps and citation opportunities. Content teams can act on those recommendations within HubSpot, deploying content agent to help them quickly generate optimized content. This keeps AEO execution connected to the workflows they already use.
Once teams are aligned on acting on AEO insights, one challenge remains: Proving that the investment is driving business results.
Enterprise stakeholders don’t want to know how many citations a campaign earned. They want to know how AEO investment is affecting pipeline, MQLs, and market share.
Most enterprise AEO programs fall short when tying AEO to revenue outcomes. Without a clear connection from brand visibility to business outcomes, AEO can be difficult to evaluate as it competes for budget against channels that have established attribution models. The work gets done, but the case for sustained investment is hard to make.
With HubSpot AEO connected to CRM data in Marketing Hub Pro and Enterprise, marketing teams can build custom reporting to see whether increases in share of voice or citations line up with changes in inbound volume, MQL rates, or pipeline.
Enterprise AEO requires infrastructure that helps teams monitor AI visibility across products and markets, coordinate content efforts, and connect visibility trends to business outcomes. As AI becomes a larger part of buyer research, centralized processes make it easier to identify gaps and act on opportunities at scale.
HubSpot AEO can support that process by bringing brand visibility, citation insights, and content recommendations into existing marketing workflows. The goal isn’t just to increase visibility, but to build a repeatable approach for managing AEO and understanding its impact on the business.

title: AEO for marketing operations: How to build scalable processes that connect AEO to revenue
content:
Buyer behavior has changed since the advent of artificial intelligence. Now, before ever filling out a form or clicking an ad, prospects are likely asking AI for recommendations, comparing vendors, and gathering answers. Those interactions shape which companies make the shortlist, but they often happen outside the systems marketing operations teams use to measure performance.
Buyers asking AI for recommendations creates a new accountability gap. The tools and processes built for search and paid traffic weren’t designed to capture how AI-assisted discovery works.
The question is how to build the infrastructure to connect AEO to the buyer journey and revenue. To make AEO measurable and actionable, marketing operations teams need to connect brand visibility data to their CRM, incorporate AI-driven touchpoints into attribution, and automate ongoing monitoring and reporting.
If AEO signals aren’t connected to the CRM, the attribution model can’t account for an important part of the buyer journey.
Marketing attribution is only as strong as the tracking infrastructure behind it. When a buyer’s first meaningful touchpoint happens inside an answer engine through a citation, a brand mention, or a recommended link, that moment typically falls outside traditional reporting.
But the more buyers use answer engines to research products, vendors, and solutions, the more the discovery journey happens before a prospect ever reaches a company’s website. In turn, its contact and pipeline data becomes more incomplete.
Consider this example: If 30% of a brand’s inbound traffic now has AI-assisted discovery as a precursor touchpoint, but the attribution model can’t capture those interactions, every revenue report will understate marketing’s influence.
Connecting AEO data to the CRM helps fix the attribution blind spot. HubSpot AEO connects visibility signals such as brand visibility score, share of voice across answer engines, and citations to contact and deal records through CRM configuration. Marketers can see which channels are driving AI-sourced traffic and map that data back to pipeline.
According to HubSpot internal data, teams who use HubSpot AEO create 78% more contacts.
Once AEO data is flowing into the CRM, the next step is building attribution logic that accounts for how AI-driven touchpoints fit into the buyer journey.
Traditional first-touch and last-touch attribution can miss the influence AI has on buyers before they ever visit a site. Even multi-touch models that rely on click data miss that influence. These models simply weren’t built for a world where a buyer gets brand context from an AI.
A buyer might ask an answer engine which vendors solve a particular problem, encounter your brand in the answer, and only later visit your website through an organic search, direct visit, or paid campaign. A click-based attribution model may credit the later interaction while missing the AI interaction that helped create awareness in the first place. That makes AEO difficult to evaluate using conventional channel reporting.
When AEO activity isn’t incorporated into attribution, there is no obvious reason to keep a channel that appears to generate little ROI. The truth is, AEO actually influenced demand earlier in the journey, but the model can’t see it.
AEO reporting can provide another layer of context. HubSpot AEO ’s Brand Visibility Dashboard surfaces how a brand is represented in answer engines over time, including share of voice trends and citation growth. Marketing teams can use those trend lines alongside CRM pipeline data to understand how changes in AEO visibility affect downstream movement.
Once AEO is part of the attribution framework, the remaining challenge is keeping the data current without creating a manual reporting burden.
AEO needs to become part of the regular reporting cadence, not a quarterly snapshot assembled manually by the operations team. Answer engines update their answers continuously, and a brand’s presence can shift week over week based on content changes, competitor moves, and new publications entering the citation pool.
One-off reporting becomes especially limiting in the face of constantly changing AI answers. If staying current requires marketers to pull data manually, update spreadsheets, and build reports from scratch, AEO quickly becomes another ad hoc request for the operations team.
Automation turns AEO into an ongoing signal. HubSpot AEO continuously tracks brand visibility score, citations, and share of voice without requiring manual pulls. Ops leaders don’t need to manually pull AEO metrics because visibility score, citations, and share of voice refresh automatically inside the tool.
For marketing operations, the opportunity is about building the infrastructure to understand how AI-assisted discovery contributes to the buyer journey, then connecting that activity to the revenue data the business already relies on. As AI becomes a more common starting point for research, teams that can connect visibility signals with contacts, pipeline, and conversion data will have a clearer picture of how buyers discover and evaluate their brand.
With tools like HubSpot AEO, marketing operations teams can bring AI visibility, citation, and share of voice data into the broader reporting workflow, making it easier to monitor changes and connect them to downstream outcomes. The infrastructure to measure AI’s influence is becoming part of the modern marketing stack; the next step is putting that infrastructure to work.

title: AEO for demand generation teams: How to generate qualified pipeline as AI reshapes buyer discovery
content:
Demand generation has been built around the assumption that buyers will come to a brand when they are ready to learn about its category, whether through search, ads, content, or other channels. The funnel starts when a prospect arrives somewhere the business can see, measure, and influence it. But AI is changing what happens before that point.
Increasingly, buyers begin their research inside AI interfaces. They ask a question, get a curated answer, and form opinions about a category before arriving on a vendor website. If your brand isn’t part of the AI-generated answer, you’re not in the conversation that shapes the shortlist.
Demand generation teams that understand the AI shift are extending their funnel. The goal is to expand the traditional funnel to ensure brand presence at this new early stage of buyer research, not replace it altogether.
Demand generation teams need to extend the funnel upstream to generate qualified pipeline as AI reshapes buyer discovery. Teams need to understand where buyers encounter their brand in AI answers, create content that reinforces those research journeys, and connect AEO performance to MQLs and pipeline.
Before demand generation teams can capture AI-driven demand, they need to map where their brand appears in AI research and where competitors appear instead of them. Start by charting the AI landscape for your category. Investigate:
Without this map, demand generation teams risk only optimizing the part of the funnel they can measure while remaining blind to the new phase where buyers now form their opinions. They may have a well-optimized inbound program while missing key research interactions that influence buyers before they become identifiable prospects.
HubSpot AEO addresses the potential optimization blind spot. The Brand Visibility Dashboard and citation analysis in HubSpot AEO help marketers see where their brand appears in AI-generated answers, organized by engine, query type, and competitive context. Teams can identify the specific prompts that drive buyers to their category but don’t surface their brand. This reveals exactly where their gaps in AI visibility and demand generation are.
The visibility into how a brand is being cited and the exact prompts driving buyers but not surfacing the brand gives teams a starting point. The next step is turning those gaps into content that helps buyers move from AI-assisted research to active evaluation.
Once teams understand their AI visibility gaps, they need to create content designed to capture AI-influenced buyers at the evaluation stage, not content that sends them back to the beginning of the funnel.
Buyers influenced by AI arrive on a website with more context than traditional inbound leads. Since an answer engine has told them that certain vendors are worth evaluating, they need content that is stronger than what typical top-of-funnel leads are looking for.
Treating AI-referred visitors like any other inbound audience can create unnecessary friction. Sending a buyer who has already researched the category to a generic awareness page or introductory ebook forces them to retrace steps they’ve already taken. Instead, demand generation teams should create content that answers the specific questions buyers use to evaluate vendors: how solutions compare, which use cases they support, what differentiates one approach from another, and what evidence supports the claims.
For example, if a buyer has already decided to evaluate three vendors based on an AI research session, a brand’s content needs to quickly reinforce why it deserves to be considered. Otherwise, competitors who also showed up in the original AI answer and then reinforced it with better content will outstrip you.
HubSpot AEO ’s Recommendations identify questions and topics that a content library isn’t adequately addressing to appear in AI search. Content agent helps demand gen teams fill those gaps quickly, producing structured content that addresses the research questions driving AI-assisted discovery, aligned with how AEO tracks citation-worthy content.
Having the right content for answer engines pays off. According to HubSpot data, businesses that use HubSpot AEO generate 2.7x more marketing qualified leads (MQLs).
But content creation alone doesn’t demonstrate business impact. Demand generation teams also need to connect AEO activity to the metrics they already use to manage performance.
Demand generation teams are accountable to MQLs, pipeline, and revenue, not to visibility scores. Making AEO a permanent line in the budget requires demonstrating that AI-assisted discovery is moving the numbers.
Measurement and attribution are challenging because AI discovery rarely happens in isolation. Buyers who first encounter a brand in an AI answer often touch multiple channels before converting. Crediting AEO in that path requires more sophisticated modeling than last-click, and most teams don’t have it built yet.
HubSpot AEO gives teams a head start on that case. Because prompt tracking can be filtered by buyer’s journey phase, teams can see whether they’re winning visibility specifically at the decision and comparison stages — the prompts closest to a buying decision — rather than just accumulating awareness-stage mentions. And because AEO’s prompt suggestions are already grounded in CRM data in Marketing Hub Pro and Enterprise, the visibility being tracked reflects real buyers, not a generic market.
Over time, teams can show leadership not just that AEO drives traffic but that it drives the right traffic, at the right intent level, with a conversion profile that justifies the investment.
The portion of a pipeline that starts with AI research will only keep growing. It’s a new part of the buyer journey that didn’t even exist a few years ago. The response isn’t to abandon paid media or content, but to extend the funnel upstream to catch relevant traffic in AI search engines.
HubSpot AEO allows demand generation teams to do just that. It provides the tools to track brand visibility, create content to fill visibility gaps, and measure the impact on leads and revenue. By bringing those insights into the broader marketing workflow, HubSpot AEO gives teams a practical way to turn AI-assisted discovery into measurable demand.

title: AEO for product marketing teams: How to ensure your positioning shows up accurately in AI results
content:
Product marketing’s core job is positioning: Deciding how a product should be described, what category it competes in, and which differentiators matter most to buyers. The results are deployed through sales, content, and campaigns. But now there’s a channel that interprets and rebroadcasts your positioning at scale without asking permission: answer engines.
When a buyer asks an AI assistant about your product category, they get a confident summary answer synthesized from hundreds of sources, including reviews, comparisons, competitor content, and industry coverage. If your owned content isn’t in that source mix, your positioning is being written for you by everyone else.
Product marketing teams with strong AEO visibility do three critical things: Actively monitor what answer engines say about their products; create the owned content that shapes those descriptions; and track whether their positioning investments change how AI represents them to buyers.
Monitoring highlights what you need to reposition and where. It’s easy to spot product positioning drift in traditional channels. You can read competitor ads, check your own landing pages, and listen to sales calls. But it’s harder with AI answers. If an answer engine draws on stale or competitor-influenced product descriptions, buyers may get inaccurate information or positioning about your product, and you may never know unless you have the right signals in place.
HubSpot AEO ’s Brand Visibility Dashboard lets teams track which prompts surface their brand and what context surrounds those citations. Marketers can monitor how their product is described across answer engines, including mentions, how the brand is framed relative to competitors, and identify specific areas where the AI narrative doesn’t match the intended positioning.
Answer engines synthesize their responses from the sources they consider most authoritative. For product positioning, that means owned content that clearly, specifically, and credibly articulates what your product does, who it’s for, and how it compares in a structured way that’s easy for answer engines to parse and excerpt.
Product marketing teams without a systematic approach to AEO content often publish marketing-heavy pages that aren’t optimized for answer engines extracting factual claims. So answer engines skip over your content and cite competitors who publish more extractable content.
HubSpot AEO ’s Recommendations tool provides specific, actionable content guidance based on your citation and visibility data. The content agent feature helps you build the customized pages and structured content that answer those queries with your positioning front and center, giving answer engines high-quality source material to draw from.
Buyers who come in with accurate expectations close faster, churn less, and require less sales education. Effective AEO can shape buyer expectations before the first touchpoint, so improving product visibility in answer engines should boost both volume and pipeline quality.
But product marketing’s contribution to pipeline quality is notoriously hard to measure, and AEO is easy to deprioritize if you can’t prove the ROI. To translate visibility scores into a revenue story, you need a measurement framework that connects AI visibility improvements to pipeline metrics.
HubSpot lets you connect brand visibility data to your CRM. Once teams build the attribution view, marketers can compare pipeline velocity, close rates, and deal quality for buyers who arrived through AI-referred channels. Over time, that gives teams the data to argue that accurate AI positioning is a valuable commercial outcome, not just a visibility metric.
The proof is in the results: HubSpot research shows AEO customers generate 2.6x more leads.
For product marketers, positioning has always been shaped by sources you don’t control. What’s changed is the scale and speed at which those sources are synthesized into the first answer buyers see. Product marketing teams that build owned content designed for AI citation can take control of their brand positioning and evolve the narrative to meet customers where they’re at.

title: AEO for marketing leaders: How to stay ahead of the shift to AI-driven discovery
content:
Marketing leadership decisions used to be about where to allocate resources between known channels like paid, content, events, and email. Each of these channels has established performance benchmarks and predictable customer acquisition cost (CAC) ranges. But now, that framework is getting harder to trust as more buyer discovery moves to answer engines.
The most valuable buyers actively researching solutions in your category are increasingly asking answer engines first. Buyers get a summary, a short list of credible vendors, and a frame for the problem before they visit anyone’s website. If your brand isn’t showing up accurately and favorably in those answers, you’re already behind.
Marketing leaders optimizing for AEO early are building AI visibility into their existing reporting stacks and connecting AEO activity to the pipeline metrics they’re already held to.
Competitive analysis in traditional search is a known discipline with established tools, benchmarks, and a shared understanding of what winning looks like. AEO competitive intelligence is newer, and most marketing leaders don’t have a clear picture of where they stand relative to their competitors in AI answers. You might be ahead, behind, or invisible in answer engines, but the marketing team has no reliable way to know.
HubSpot AEO ’s Brand Visibility Dashboard includes share of voice, which shows how a brand’s citation frequency compares to competitors across the prompts that matter to their category. The brand visibility score gives a single number to track over time, while the competitive view shows if that number represents a lead, a lag, or a gap that needs closing.
Once you have a visibility data foundation, you can make the investment case by connecting metrics to investment and return.
Stakeholders usually view new channels as experimental, so initial investment is usually small, attribution is unclear, and the ask gets deprioritized against channels with cleaner ROI stories. That’s where AEO is in most marketing organizations right now. But competitors moving earlier already have compounding brand authority that’s expensive to overcome.
If a competitor earns consistent citations for the 10 prompts that describe your category, buyers will see them as the default answer. HubSpot AEO gives teams the data to build a real business case: Current brand visibility score, share of voice against named competitors, citation trends over time, and recommendations for which specific investments will close the gap. With solid data, teams can present leadership with a gap, a trajectory, and a plan.
According to HubSpot’s internal research, AEO customers generate 2.7x more MQLs.
Once there’s buy-in for AEO, teams need to show ROI by tying activity to the revenue outcomes.
Marketing leaders who can’t connect AEO to revenue outcomes will eventually face the same pressure that hits every new channel: Prove it or cut it. Leadership wants to know whether the investment changed pipeline velocity, increased MQL volume, or improved close rates, so the measurement framework needs to speak that language from the start.
HubSpot lets teams connect AEO performance to their CRM data. Once marketers tag AI-referred contacts and build the reporting views, teams can track how buyers who discovered the brand through answer engines move through the pipeline, from first AI-referred visit to MQL to closed deal. That puts the answer in the same reporting stack leadership already reviews, rather than a separate tool.
The window to build AEO into your marketing infrastructure successfully is narrower than it looks. Establish measurement and competitive baselines now, so you have the data advantage when the board starts asking why the organic pipeline looks different than it did three years ago.

title: AEO for growth marketing teams: How to find scalable acquisition channels when paid and organic plateau
content:
Growth marketing is all about finding the next channel opportunity before the current one gets crowded and expensive. Paid search got crowded. Content took time. Email got filtered. The teams that found a new lever early on took advantage of lower competition, cost, and disproportionate returns before the channel normalized.
Right now, AI-driven discovery is that window of opportunity. Buyers are already using answer engines to research software categories, compare vendors, and form opinions about who the credible players are. Brands earning citations consistently are building awareness before buyers ever hit a landing page, and most of their competitors haven’t noticed yet.
Growth marketing teams need to connect AEO to acquisition metrics quickly enough to act on the signal and justify investment. The teams doing that now are building a playbook that will be much harder to replicate once the channel matures.
Not all answer engines send the same kind of traffic. The buyer who discovers your brand through a Perplexity comparison is at a different stage than one who finds you in a general answer about your category. Knowing which answer engines drive the highest-intent visitors is the starting point for AEO resource allocation.
Growth teams that don’t know the sources of their AI-referred traffic treat AEO as a single channel and optimize generically. They waste resources spreading effort across engines, whether they send buyers or not. HubSpot AEO ’s Brand Visibility Dashboard and citation analysis break down where your brand appears by engine and query type, so you can see which prompts drive the most valuable traffic.
Once teams know where the highest-converting AI traffic originates, marketers can focus on how to produce enough content to capture demand at scale.
AEO-ready content is specific and structured, and directly answers well-defined questions in formats that answer engines can excerpt and cite. But it takes more than a quarterly blog to build meaningful share of voice across a category.
To dominate category questions before competitors, growth teams need a faster content cadence than traditional brand awareness campaigns. Content agent in HubSpot is built to create the content types and structures that earn AEO citations. Paired with Recommendations, which identify the specific questions and formats your content library is missing, content agent scales production in a targeted way, addressing content gaps with the highest citation potential.
When HubSpot AEO tells you what to create, content agent drafts a research-backed blog post using your brand voice, ICP data, and real citation data. Your CRM data informs smarter prompts, content agent handles the research and writing, and you publish without switching platforms.
Scale matters, but it’s only worth it if you can attribute the results. To do that, teams need to connect AEO activity to acquisition metrics.
Growth marketing teams live in acquisition data like cost per lead (CPL), customer acquisition costs (CAC), conversion rates, and pipeline velocity. To warrant sustained investment over experimentation, AEO needs to show up in those terms.
HubSpot’s data model lets you connect AEO visibility to contact and deal records. Once you tag AI-referred contacts and build the reporting views, you can track how AI-referred visitors move through your acquisition funnel, from first touch to MQL to deal. Because that attribution can then sit in the same reporting system as paid and organic, teams can compare channel efficiency without exporting data to a separate tool.
The growth channel window for AEO won’t stay open indefinitely. As more teams figure out what drives citations, it will get harder to build share. Teams that build measurement and production infrastructure now will have the performance data and operational advantage when the channel becomes competitive.

title: AEO for digital marketing teams: How to ensure your brand is visible across every channel
content:
Digital marketing teams have spent years building integrated measurement, connecting paid, organic, social, and email into a single picture of how buyers move through the funnel. That picture now has a gap. A growing share of buyer discovery happens in AI interfaces that don’t show up cleanly in any existing channel report.
AEO has a way of landing in organizations without a clear owner. SEO thinks it belongs to content, content thinks it belongs to SEO, and demand gen is watching paid customer acquisition costs (CAC) rise while organic traffic flattens with no clear answer to either problem. Meanwhile, buyers are already using answer engines to shortlist vendors.
Digital marketing teams that get AEO working integrate it into their existing workstream. Visibility tracking lives alongside existing channel dashboards, AEO recommendations are surfaced directly into the content calendar, and attribution is connected to the same pipeline reports the team already uses.
Most marketing teams already juggle a dozen channel dashboards. When AEO data lives in the same reporting stack, it becomes part of everyday decision-making instead of another report to check. Content, demand gen, and leadership see AI visibility shifts as they happen, with no manual pulls required.
HubSpot’s AEO dashboard gives teams a brand visibility score, trended over time across ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity. With Marketing Hub Professional or Enterprise, that data lives in the same platform as the rest of your marketing reporting, so AI visibility can come up in the same weekly review as CPL and conversion rates.
Having visibility in one place creates the foundation. Acting on it requires coordinating AEO recommendations with the team that actually produces and publishes content.
Content calendars are already full, so AEO works best when it fits into the planning process the team already uses. When AEO guidance shows up directly inside content planning, teams can optimize each page once for both audiences, skip the prioritization tug-of-war, and act on recommendations consistently. Coverage gaps and optimization opportunities get addressed as part of regular planning instead of piling up in a separate tool.
HubSpot AEO recommendations connect directly to HubSpot’s content tools, so your team can act on them without leaving the platform. Content agent can draft content for the specific gaps a recommendation identifies, and teams can review and edit before publishing. That keeps AEO work in step with the editorial process a team already follows, with production aimed more precisely at what matters.
Coordination makes execution more efficient; the measurement layer is what lets you report the impact to leadership with confidence.
Digital marketing teams are accountable to KPIs that don’t yet have a standard AEO line item like CPL, MQL volume, pipeline influenced, or revenue attributed. Making the case for AEO investment requires translating visibility metrics into the language leadership already uses.
Without connected reporting between AEO activity and pipeline outcomes, the channel gets treated as brand investment with fuzzy returns. That’s a defensible position once, but not across multiple planning cycles when other channels have cleaner attribution.
HubSpot Smart CRM tracks AI Referrals as its own traffic source, so contacts that arrive from AI answers carry that source onto their records and the deals they’re associated with. Pair that with your brand visibility score in HubSpot AEO , and you can connect what’s happening in answer engines to leads and pipeline. It’s a new data layer in the reporting your team already reviews, not a separate scorecard to maintain.
Digital marketing teams that integrate AEO into their existing measurement and editorial processes now will have both the operational infrastructure and the attribution story when AI-assisted discovery becomes a primary channel for their buyers. The advantage compounds the earlier teams start building the baseline.

title: AEO for content strategists: How to move the needle on citations
content:
Content strategists already know how to build for search. They understand how to map topics, connect related pages, and create enough depth to establish authority. But answer engine optimization (AEO) begs the question: When buyers ask ChatGPT, Gemini, or Perplexity about your category, which pages, if any, actually get cited?
AEO doesn’t make your existing search strategy obsolete, but it does add a new measurement layer that shows how your brand and content appear in AI-generated answers. That includes prompt coverage, brand visibility, citations, and competitor performance.
For content strategists, that means deciding which pages need updates, where coverage is missing, and whether those changes improve visibility over time.
Start with a baseline. HubSpot recommends tracking your AEO metrics before and after you make changes so you can measure and compare their impact over time. HubSpot AEO runs tracked prompts daily across ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity and aggregates the results into visibility and citation data.
Use citation analysis to see which domains, pages, and content types answer engines reference for your tracked prompts. You can compare your owned domain citation rate with competitors, review your top owned citations, and identify gaps where competitors are cited more often.
Then, use recommendations to decide what to address first. HubSpot AEO generates recommendations using citation patterns across your tracked prompts; it assigns a content type, channel, and priority to each one. That turns the audit into a prioritized list of pages that content strategists can update and content gaps they can fill.
According to HubSpot data , 92% of industry-specific content pages were cited by answer engines, generating a 49% lift in AI visibility.
Use your audit findings to identify pages that need clearer answers and topics with thin coverage. HubSpot’s AEO guidance emphasizes clear content structure, direct answers, accurate brand information, authority, consistency, and cross-channel presence.
That means a strong SEO content library is still useful, but it may need targeted AEO updates. Instead of expanding every topic cluster, focus on the pages and content types connected to prompts where your brand has weaker visibility or competitors earn more citations.
HubSpot AEO recommendations can surface owned content, social amplification, and outreach opportunities based on citation patterns in your tracked prompts. In Marketing Hub Professional and Enterprise, Super Admins can opt eligible accounts into the beta, which generates blog posts from owned content recommendations with the content agent. Users can review and edit the draft before publishing.
Measure the same AEO metrics before and after you make content changes. Answer engine responses change over time, and HubSpot recommends reviewing performance across multiple days or weeks before evaluating trends or drawing conclusions.
In HubSpot AEO, you can track your brand visibility score over time, compare your visibility with competitors, analyze citation trends, and monitor prompt performance. On the Owned content insights tab, the Estimated impact report shows the estimated citation impact of acting on all recommendations for that channel.
Use that data to decide what to tackle next. You do not need to rebuild your entire content program for AEO. Start with the content you already have, make targeted changes based on visibility and citation data, and measure what changes before planning the next round of work.
